title: A Veil for the Wolf Anew
premise: Lena Winterbourne, cartographer of the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that a feral child who speaks a dead tongue is not a stray but a living map — the last fragment of Vael, a country erased from existence by a bargain its people made to survive. The Guild's masters want to harvest him to reopen trade with the vanished realm; Lena, who owes her own life to a similar erasure, chooses instead to help him find the door out. Hunted through folded geographies and betrayed by the mentor who raised her, Lena must decide whether restoring Vael means unmaking the world that replaced it — including herself. In the end she pays the price of survival in reverse: she gives up her own mapped self so the boy can carry his country's memory into the new world, and the found family they gathered along the way becomes the country that no longer needs a door.
about_author: Odile Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer appear on any chart. She writes fantasy about borders, bargains, and the people who fall between them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Vanishings
chapters.summary: POV Lena. In the Guild's counting house, Lena balances ledgers of traded impossibilities while hiding that her own name appears nowhere in the world's records. A soaked, silent child is left at the door during a storm, clutching a compass that points at nothing. Emotional beat: wary tenderness — she recognizes a fellow unmapped thing.

chapters.title: A Tongue Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Lena, with fragments from the boy's memory. The child speaks a language predating every kingdom; only the Guild's oldest ledger can half-translate it. He names himself Ash and says one word repeatedly: 'Vael.' The Guild masters take sudden, hungry interest. Emotional beat: dread blooming beneath curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Compass Points At
chapters.summary: POV Ash. Through his eyes we see the Guild as a place of cages dressed as kindness. His compass needle spins toward a wall that isn't a wall — the seam where Vael was folded out of the world. Lena secretly follows the same bearing on her charts. Emotional beat: two lonely people orbiting the same hidden door.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Her mentor, Magister Corvane, reveals the truth: Vael bargained itself out of existence to escape a devouring war, leaving one child behind as collateral and key. The Guild intends to spend Ash to reopen the trade route. Corvane reminds Lena he bought her survival too. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into debt.

chapters.title: Thieves of Geography
chapters.summary: POV alternating Lena/Ash. Lena steals the old ledgers and flees with Ash into the city's folded alleys, gathering unlikely allies: a disgraced bridge-toll witch, Sable, and a smuggler who once sold a river. The Guild posts impossible bounties. Emotional beat: first breath of chosen family.

chapters.title: Where the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Ash. Following the compass, the fugitives cross into places where erased Vael bleeds through — streets that echo, bread that tastes of a dead harvest. Ash begins remembering his country and fears that finding the door means losing himself inside it. Emotional beat: grief as homecoming.

chapters.title: The Toll Nobody Named
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Sable's bridge demands payment in identity: each crossing shaves something true from the traveler. Lena learns what she already suspected — she was born in Vael, an infant smuggled out before the erasure, which is why no record holds her. Emotional beat: identity shattered and strangely freed.

chapters.title: Corvane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Cornered by Guild hunters, the group is saved only when Corvane arrives — not to arrest them, but to argue: reopening Vael will unmake everyone born in its absence, thousands of lives against one nation. He offers Lena her name back if she surrenders Ash. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Ash, climax. At the seam, Ash can open the door — but entering means dissolving into Vael's restoration, alone forever. Instead he turns the compass inward and offers the door to Lena, the other last child of Vael. She refuses to be restored at anyone's cost; together they break the compass, choosing the present over the erased past. Emotional beat: refusal as salvation.

chapters.title: A Country of the Living
chapters.summary: POV Lena, resolution. The Guild fractures; Corvane, holding the broken compass, quietly lets them go. Lena, Sable, the smuggler, and Ash make a household above a map shop, drawing charts of places that exist and some that might again. Ash teaches them his language one word at a time. Emotional beat: found family as the only country worth mapping.
